title: Computer vision
blurb: How current vision models learn from images and text, find and segment objects, pair with LLMs, generate images and rebuild 3D scenes.

main.title: Stanford CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
main.why: Detection and segmentation, video, self-supervised learning, generative models, 3D and vision-language. In English.

main.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
main.why: ViT. A plain Transformer on image patches rivals CNNs when pretrained on enough data.

main.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
main.why: CLIP. Matching 400M images to their captions gives zero-shot classification from text prompts.

further.title: SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features

main.title: DINOv3
main.why: Self-supervised vision encoder whose frozen features beat specialized models, with Gram anchoring keeping dense features clean.

main.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
main.why: A proposal network shares the detector's features, making region proposals nearly free.

main.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
main.why: One network predicts all boxes and classes in a single pass, at 45 frames per second.

main.title: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
main.why: DETR. A Transformer outputs the set of objects directly, with no anchors or non-maximum suppression.

main.title: Ultralytics YOLO26: Unified Real-Time End-to-End Vision Models
main.why: The widely deployed YOLO family made NMS-free, with detection, segmentation and pose in one real-time pipeline.

main.title: Segment Anything
main.why: A promptable model trained on 1 billion masks segments new images and tasks zero-shot.

main.title: SAM 3: Segment Anything with Concepts
main.why: A noun phrase or example image finds, segments and tracks every matching object in images and video.

main.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
main.why: LLaVA. A linear layer feeds CLIP image features into an LLM, tuned on GPT-4-written instructions.

main.title: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
main.why: A SigLIP 2 encoder feeds images and video through an MLP into Qwen3 LLMs, with 256K-token context.

main.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
main.why: The basis of Stable Diffusion. Diffusion in an autoencoder's latent space, with cross-attention for text.

main.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
main.why: DiT. A Transformer replaces the U-Net, and image quality keeps rising with compute.

main.title: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
main.why: Stable Diffusion 3. Rectified flow training and MM-DiT, a Transformer with separate text and image weights.

main.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
main.why: An MLP maps a 3D point and view direction to color and density, rendered into new views.

main.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
main.why: Optimized 3D Gaussians, splatted rather than ray-marched, render 1080p views in real time.

main.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
main.why: One forward pass predicts cameras, depth and point maps from many views, often beating optimization-based methods.
Off-the-shelf CLIP and BLIP failed on short product queries, so embeddings tuned on the catalog now rank ads.
OCR plus an LLM transcribes menu photos, and a guardrail model sends the doubtful ones to humans.
